output.name: Tulmesk

anatomy.part: lantern hung from the halyard at the top of the rope
masthead, where the rope and sail meet
belly of the sail, its outward curve to the left
amidships on the deck, foot of the mast
stern of the hull, high on the left
lowest point of the keel, under the hull
bow tip, raised on the right
lit fish of the shoal, hanging beneath the boat

output.myth: When the first boats went out past the Leeward edge, a crew of nine stayed fishing too long. Dark came down with no moon, and their hull broke on the rocks where the Unflown begins. They went under with the mast still standing. Under the wreck a shoal of small fish had been feeding on the scraps, and when the boat went down they did a foolish, kind thing: they lit their own bodies, every one, and hung beneath the hull like a lamp. Sil saw the glow from the Drowned Lantern and came down to look. Kael cast his net for the lights and, as always, caught nothing. The lights are still burning in Vel. Old women say a drowned man can find the way down by them, and a living one can find the way home. If you see a shoal lit under a boat, do not net it. Tie your knots twice, and say the crew's names.
output.verse:
Small fish under hull,
they lit their own bodies low,
and still burn in Vel.
